 Print Tamil Nadu holiday announcement: Schools and colleges closed on November 9, November 28 a working day Tamil Nadu holiday November 9 : The Tamil Nadu government has declared November 9 a holiday for all government offices, public sector undertakings, schools, colleges and educational institutions across the state. The decision was announced on Wednesday following requests from students, parents, teachers and government employees planning to travel to their hometowns for Deepavali, which falls on November 8. According to an official release, November 28 will be observed as a working day to compensate for the additional holiday. The arrangement allows people to travel for the festival while ensuring that the lost working day is accounted for in the state's official calendar. Why has Tamil Nadu declared a holiday? The government said the decision followed representations from students, parents, teachers and government employees who are expected to travel to their native places to celebrate Deepavali. With the festival falling on November 8, the additional holiday on November 9 is intended to accommodate travel plans. The closure will cover government offices, public sector undertakings, schools, colleges and other educational institutions throughout Tamil Nadu. November 28 has been designated as a working day to make up for the holiday. Treasury services to remain operational The government clarified that the November 9 holiday does not fall under the provisions of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Consequently, district collectors have been instructed to ensure that treasuries and sub-treasuries in every district remain operational with essential staff. The arrangement is intended to ensure that urgent government-related financial and administrative work can continue despite the holiday. District authorities have been asked to make the necessary staffing arrangements to handle essential tasks. November 28 to be a working day Government offices and educational institutions covered by the announcement will remain closed on November 9, while November 28 will function as a regular working day to compensate for the additional holiday. Students, parents, teachers and government employees should take note of the revised schedule when planning travel and work commitments around Deepavali. The government release specifies the institutions covered by the holiday and the arrangements required to maintain essential treasury services across the state.
